laws.rule: Mount Etna's summit area is divided into a Summit Zone (around the summit craters and generally above 2,500 m) and, inside it, a Permanent Hazard Zone around the active craters, where access is always under specific safety rules. When Sicily's civil protection department declares the pre-alarm phase the Permanent Hazard Zone is closed; at the alarm phase the whole Summit Zone is closed. The access rules themselves are set by mayoral ordinances of the towns around the volcano.

layers.process: On Stromboli, walking up the volcano is free to 290 m above sea level on the Stromboli side and to 130 m on the Ginostra side (Punta Corvi path). Above those heights, up to 400 m, only with authorised mountain or volcano guides. Above 290 m, hikers must wear a certified mountain helmet and a dust mask (the guides provide them), and sign a release. Each guide may take at most 25 people, and no more than 75 people may be above 290 m at once. The Sentiero Natura path was closed under this ordinance. The ordinance modifies Ordinance n. 50 of 14 August 2024 and may have been replaced; the guide agencies and the Comune di Lipari civil protection service hold the current version.
